terms.meaning: A map of what connects to what, without the true distances or shapes.
A connection point on a facility where a circuit begins or ends.
A single electrical or fibre route between two terminals.
A structure, such as a tower or carrier, that more than one circuit uses.
An identifier used by the source to group coverage. This file does not define it, so its exact meaning is not stated here.

depends_on: Python standard library math and urllib.parse

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header and imports
sections.what: States the rule that no connections are invented here and that diagram coordinates are not real coordinates. Brings in the libraries used for checking numbers and web addresses.
sections.why: Likely reason: the header warns future readers that the display is not a survey.
sections.watch_out: Do not add inferred links or treat diagram positions as geographic data.

sections.name: Strict
sections.title: Strict base record
sections.what: Sets the shared rules for every record in this file: unknown fields are rejected and infinite or missing numbers are rejected.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents silent data drift and stops bad numbers from entering the display.

sections.name: NetworkSource
sections.title: Source document record
sections.what: Describes one source document with its identifier, file hash, file name, location within the file, how well it was qualified, and the links used to view it. Links are only accepted if they are local review addresses.
sections.why: Likely reason: every displayed item must point at a document the reviewer can open, and nothing may link outside the local machine.
sections.watch_out: Links that are not local or that contain credentials are rejected, so changing a link format can break the whole network.

sections.name: Facility
sections.title: Facility record
sections.what: Describes one facility with its name, status, diagram position, the sources that support it and a stated limitation.
sections.why: Likely reason: facilities are the anchor points that circuits and terminals attach to.
sections.watch_out: The diagram position is display only and must not be read as a real location.

sections.name: Terminal
sections.title: Terminal record
sections.what: Describes a connection point that belongs to one facility, with its name, how it is associated, its sources and any unresolved question.
sections.why: Likely reason: terminals let circuits attach to a specific point at a facility.
sections.watch_out: A terminal pointing at a missing facility makes the whole network fail.

sections.name: ActivityRef
sections.title: Activity reference
sections.what: Holds a simple pointer to one activity by project and activity identifier, so a circuit or asset can say which schedule work it belongs to.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the network linked to the schedule without copying schedule data.

sections.name: Circuit
sections.title: Circuit record
sections.what: Describes one electrical or fibre route, including its two terminals, the identifiers it involves, its sources, diagram points, its scope, any unresolved question, linked activities and any shared carrier.
sections.why: Likely reason: circuits are the main connections the reader wants to see, so each needs its own traceable record.
sections.watch_out: An undated circuit is not allowed to carry construction dates, and its endpoints must sit on the facility positions.

sections.name: PICoverage
sections.title: PI coverage record
sections.what: Records, for one PI identifier, which project covers it, how well the documents cover it, how it is shown and what is still unresolved.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It appears to show which projects are accounted for in the network.
sections.watch_out: Each PI may appear only once across the coverage rows.

sections.name: StationAsset
sections.title: Station physical asset record
sections.what: Describes one physical item inside a station, such as a breaker, voltage transformer, switch or mast, with its position, size, configuration, sources, reason for display and linked activities.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a station view show individual equipment with its own evidence.
sections.watch_out: The size values must be positive, and the configuration must exist in the station's list of configurations.

sections.name: InventoryRow
sections.title: Inventory row
sections.what: Records one family of equipment, what the source claims, what is shown and what is left out, with the sources behind it.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes clear what the station drawing does not show, so nobody assumes it is complete.

sections.name: StationView
sections.title: Station view record
sections.what: Describes one station drawing: its facility, width and depth, how those were measured, its configurations, its assets, its inventory, what was kept from scope and its sources.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each station drawing tied to its facility and its evidence.
sections.watch_out: Width and depth must be positive, and the basis note must be kept honest about how the size was obtained.

sections.name: ProgrammeNetwork
sections.title: Whole network consistency checks
sections.what: Assembles every record type into the network and runs a long set of checks: no duplicate identities, every terminal and station belongs to a known facility, circuits meet their facilities, shared carriers resolve, undated circuits do not borrow dates, and every source reference resolves. It also checks that each PI appears once.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops a network from being shown when any link in the evidence chain is broken.
sections.watch_out: One unresolved reference anywhere blocks the entire network, so check the error text first when a load fails.

summary: Defines the data shapes for the diagram-style network view: facilities, terminals, circuits, station layouts and their sources, and checks that every link in it is backed by a document reference.
purpose: Holds the display topology so the app can draw facilities and their connections, separate from schedule dates and from any real survey coordinates.
why: The file header states the rules: no connections are inferred, every connection carries a document reference, and diagram positions must never be treated as surveyed or IFC coordinates.
how: Each record type describes one kind of thing: a source document, a facility, a terminal at a facility, an activity reference, a circuit between two terminals, a coverage row for an identifier called PI, a physical asset in a station, an inventory row and a station view. The final network record gathers all of them and runs a reconcile check: identities must be unique, every terminal must belong to a known facility, every circuit must have real endpoints that sit on their facility's diagram position, and every source reference must resolve.
inputs: Plain data from the network source, validated against these record types. Each source link must be a local review address or a relative review asset path.
outputs: A validated network object, or an error naming the first failed rule.
risks: Strict settings reject unknown fields and non-finite numbers. Any unresolved source reference blocks the whole network. Diagram positions are display only, so changing them does not change real geography.
debug: Read the error message, which names the failed rule. Check that the identifiers used in terminals, circuits and station views exist in their lists, and that source identifiers match the sources list.
